key_insight: Flow-rate statistics in disordered porous media are governed by local topological splitting and merging, leading pore-body fluxes to follow a Gamma distribution that also determines throat fluxes.
engineering_relevance: This provides a compact, geometry-based way to predict transport in porous media from minimal structural information, improving design and analysis of filters, catalysts, and subsurface flows.
method: Built a pore-network model for steady Stokes flow in 2D disordered arrays of circular obstacles
Included local flow-rate correlations arising from flow splitting and merging
Linked the Gamma distribution parameter to geometric variability, especially the coefficient of variation of pore-throat widths
evidence_signal: The theory is validated against computational fluid dynamics simulations and outperforms prior mean-field models that ignore local flow-rate correlations.
watch_item: The result is derived for steady Stokes flow in two-dimensional disordered obstacle arrays, so care is needed when extending it to inertial, transient, or strongly three-dimensional porous systems.
paper_title: Topological origin of flow distributions in disordered porous media
